summary: This is the heart of the parrot-feeding program: a while loop that keeps asking you for seeds until the total the parrot has eaten reaches its capacity of 10.

lines.text: The loop's condition is checked before every pass, so feeding continues only while the running total is still short of capacity; once fed reaches 10 the loop ends on its own without any counter to manage.
Because `input` always hands back text, `int` converts what you typed into a number you can add up, and the prompt recomputes `capacity-fed` each time so it always reflects how much room is left.
`max(0, feed)` quietly guards against a negative entry: the parrot cannot un-eat its food, so anything below zero contributes nothing to the total.
The two variables are easy to confuse: `feed` is the amount from this one round, while `fed` is the running total that the loop condition watches.
